title: Grapheme clusters follow UAX #29 extended grapheme clusters
cm6: @marijn/find-cluster-break 1.0.4 joins a code point of its table (Unicode 17.0 Extend and SpacingMark below U+30000), anything next to a ZWJ, and regional-indicator pairs (mirrors/marijn/find-cluster-break/src/index.js:45-66). So a Hangul syllable written as jamo splits into its letters, an Indic conjunct breaks after the virama, a Prepend character stands alone, tag sequences (the flag of England) and variation selectors at or above U+E0100 (ideographic variants) split from their base, CR LF inside a string is two clusters, a control takes a following mark, and a ZWJ joins whatever follows it. The 181 fixtures of state.findClusterBreak.B9 record these.
better: The cursor, deletion, columns and word lookup never stop inside what the person editing sees as one character: the extended grapheme clusters of UAX #29 (rules GB3 to GB9c, GB11 to GB13), at the Unicode version of cm6's table or later, so that no character cm6 groups is split.
basis: Unicode Standard Annex #29, the rule native text systems and the shapers of the surfaces use (the harness's Node gives it through Intl.Segmenter, ICU 78.3, Unicode 17.0, and docs/parity/ferrum-state/oracle/cm6/text/s4-fix5.ts recorded where it differs from cm6). cm6's reason is its stack: a small table shipped in a JavaScript bundle; its README promises only extending characters, ZWJ and flags.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch that replaces findClusterBreak in the harness by one built on Intl.Segmenter; GraphemeBreakTest.txt of the same Unicode version against the patched cm6 and against Ferrum.
note: To gather before it is made (rust-researcher): the Unicode version of the Rust implementation against 17.0 (a crate, or tables generated from the UCD: a library choice of D2); what `include_extending == false` means under the full rule (cm6 uses it for backspace, commands.ts:581-585, where it removes one mark, and today also one jamo); whether any sequence cm6 groups would split (ZWJ before a non-pictograph), which the floor forbids. Risk: low once the floor is shown; one function and one table change. Adopting it at design time was weighed and lost: docs/decisions/ferrum-state.md, 2026-11-13.

title: `wordChars` matched by character, not by UTF-16 code unit
cm6: makeCategorizer compares each UTF-16 code unit of `wordChars` with the string (mirrors/cm6/state/src/charcategory.ts:32), so an astral entry makes every character that shares one of its surrogates a word character (fixtures/state.jsonl F0299).
better: A character is a word character when it is listed, and only then: selecting by word and word motion do not treat unrelated emoji or rare ideographs as letters.
basis: cm6's own documentation: "characters explicitly listed in the local language's wordChars" (mirrors/cm6/state/src/state.ts:369). The code-unit match is JavaScript string indexing.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to makeCategorizer that iterates code points.
note: Small and local. To check before adoption: no mirrored consumer passes an astral `wordChars` (lang-css "-", lang-javascript "$").

title: Transaction extenders contribute once when a filter returns specs
cm6: Extenders run once more for a transaction whose filter returned specs, and their effects and annotations are added again (mirrors/cm6/state/src/transaction.ts:352, :387).
better: An extension that adds an effect sees it once per transaction.
basis: None verified yet: no comment, CHANGELOG entry or test of cm6 says which is meant.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to transaction.ts, if adopted.
note: Needs a cm6-researcher reading of the CHANGELOG and of the consumers of duplicated effects before it can be called better.

title: Typed inputs cm6 accepts unchecked are validated alike
cm6: A change filter's ranges are used unsorted and unchecked; a range with `from > to` is kept; `update` with unsorted `add` fails on an empty set, and on a non-empty one only when the ranges that do not fit its layers reach an empty layer out of order, which depends on how the set's layers happen to be built (`state.cm6.183.d1`); which path reports a length mismatch between change sets varies, and operands with a zero-length unchanged section fail although their lengths agree.
better: A caller's mistake fails at the call that makes it, the same way on every path, instead of producing a state that fails later or silently.
basis: None beyond consistency; each case needs its own reading.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: Per case: a patch adding the check to cm6.
note: Risk: a check added where a consumer relies on the unchecked path (the view maps selections through replacements that give `from > to`). Each case is evaluated on the values the crates above pass. Added 2026-11-27, a case of Ferrum's own precondition with the same shape: a change position inside a character (D1) given to `EditorState::update` or `EditorState::changes` is not checked there; it panics later, where the new document is first computed (`Transaction::new_doc`, `Transaction::state`, often in another component's call), while cm6 checks a change's range at `ChangeSet.of` inside `update`. Evaluated with the rest of this row.

title: `RangeSet::map` maps the ranges of a chunk a change covers
cm6: A chunk wholly covered by a change is dropped without mapping its ranges, and the drop rule of Chunk.map applies only in chunks a change touches (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:151, :300-330), so whether a range survives a large replacement depends on the chunk layout.
better: Whether a decoration or marker survives an edit depends on the edit and its map mode, not on how many ranges were stored before it.
basis: None verified: the skip is an optimization of cm6 and may be intended.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to rangeset.ts, if adopted.
note: Cost: the skip is what keeps mapping a large set cheap; needs the benchmark of gate G8.

title: Range sets and cursors beyond 1,000,000,000 positions
cm6: `C.Far = 1e9` is the end sentinel and bound of range sets (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:98).
better: Documents above about 954 MiB of text can carry decorations. With positions in bytes (D1) the bound is reached at fewer characters than in cm6 for non-ASCII text, which is below the floor for such a document.
basis: The goal of large documents (docs/foundation/ferrum-foundation.md §1); the bound is a JavaScript small-integer convenience.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: The sentinel is visible in cursor output, so a patch that raises `C.Far`.
note: No consumer in sight edits a document of that size; the README lists the limit meanwhile.

title: `count_column` and `find_column` are inverse at a tab followed by an extending character
cm6: The two functions step a tab followed by an extending code point or ZWJ differently (mirrors/cm6/state/src/column.ts:8-10, :28-29; fixtures/text.jsonl F0482, F0485).
better: Rectangular selection and column motion land on the same column both ways.
basis: None verified beyond the two functions being documented as counterparts.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to column.ts; evaluated together with state.imp.001, which changes the same stepping.

title: A state whose lines hold the separator survives the JSON round trip
cm6: `toJSON` writes the document as one string and `fromJSON` splits it again, so a document built from lines that contain the separator comes back with other lines, and with a `"\r\n"` separator a shorter length (fixtures/state.jsonl F2093, F2094).
better: Saving and restoring a state gives the same document.
basis: None verified: only documents built by hand through `Text::of` are affected.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch, if adopted; it would change the JSON form, which cm6 clients read.
note: Changing the JSON form costs interchange with cm6; validating lines in `Text::of` costs a scan cm6 avoids.

title: Calls that take a position from outside the program can fail without a panic
cm6: cm6 throws a RangeError that a caller can catch.
better: An application that receives positions it cannot check first (a late LSP answer, a collaboration peer) handles the failure instead of crashing.
basis: D13 records this as what the panic contract gives up.
when: the specification of ferrum-view, or the first consumer that shows the need, whichever comes first
reference: Written tests; the fallible variants add to the API and displace nothing.
note: Adding them later breaks no caller (D13).

title: A document structure that keeps very long lines cheap
cm6: `Text` is a tree of lines; one line is one string, so an edit in a line of many megabytes copies it (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts).
better: Minified or generated files with enormous lines edit as fast as others.
basis: The goal of native performance; no measurement yet.
when: gate G8 of ferrum-state conformance, on a benchmark with long lines
reference: None needed if the observable behavior is unchanged; `Text::children` exposes the shape, so a change of shape is observable.
note: D2 keeps cm6's tree because nothing measured shows it missing a target.

title: Short forms of the calls whose cm6 defaults are the common case
cm6: cm6's optional parameters let a caller write `EditorSelection.cursor(pos)`, `EditorSelection.range(anchor, head)`, `doc.sliceString(from)`, `changes.mapPos(pos)`, `state.update({changes: {from, insert}})`.
better: Not above cm6: this is where Ferrum is below it for the developer. D14 makes every optional parameter required, so the same calls are `EditorSelection::cursor(pos, 0, None, None)`, `EditorSelection::range(anchor, head, None, None, 0)`, `ChangeSpec::Change { from, to: None, insert: Some("x".into()) }`. Short forms (functions with the defaults applied, `From` conversions into the spec types) would give back cm6's brevity.
basis: D14 records this as what required parameters give up and names the port of `@codemirror/commands` as the evidence that reopens it; the skeleton of 2026-11-14 shows the forms.
when: the specification of ferrum-commands, which counts the call patterns of cm6's commands; earlier if the port of ferrum-view shows one pattern at more than a hundred call sites
reference: Written tests that each short form equals the full call; the short forms add to the API and displace nothing.
note: Adding them later breaks no caller (D14). Which forms is decided from counts of cm6's call sites, not chosen in advance.

title: A tab size of 0 refused where it is configured
cm6: `EditorState.tabSize` takes any number (mirrors/cm6/state/src/state.ts:267, the facet `tabSize`); `countColumn` and `findColumn` then compute with `NaN` at the first tab (mirrors/cm6/state/src/column.ts:8-10, :26-31), so columns are silently wrong.
better: Ferrum already panics at the first column computation whatever the string holds (`state.cm6.216.d1`, Q85). Refusing a tab size of 0 when the state is created or reconfigured would put the failure where the application wrote the value, instead of in the first column computation of the view or a command.
basis: D13 (a panic guards a condition its caller can test); the decision on Q85, docs/decisions/ferrum-state.md, "The pilot review of the implementation".
reference: cm6 with `tabSize` checked at `EditorState.create` and `reconfigure`; every other output unchanged.
note: Whether the facet's combine may panic is checked at the delta; it touches no public signature.

title: `compare` reports a changed split between ranges after an edit in one coordinate space
cm6: `compare` sets the flag that calls `boundChange` when `a.openEnd(end) != b.openEnd(end)` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:889), where `end` is a position of the new document and side A's `activeTo` are positions of the old one; after a change that alters the length (`dPos` != 0) A's open count is measured at the wrong place. Run on cm6 6.7.6 with `a.openEnd(end - dPos)` instead: 9 of the 394 fixtures of chunk `rangeset` change (F5006, F5009, F5019, F5024, F5033, F5036, F5040, F5078, F5081), each in its `bound` records only, the `range` and `point` records unchanged. cm6 misses `boundChange(6)` in F5009 and `boundChange(55)` in F5019, and reports calls the corrected code does not make in six others (one in F5006, more than a hundred in F5081).
better: The view learns of every place where the split of decorations changed after an edit, and of no other (`mirrors/cm6/view/src/docview.ts:637`, `:650` turn each call into a range to redraw): no stale split is left in the rendering, and no redraw is asked for nothing. In Ferrum it also makes `compare`'s calls independent of the position unit, so that they convert exactly from cm6's on non-ASCII text, which they cannot while the mixed comparison stays (`state.cm6.188.d2`).
basis: cm6's own documentation of `boundChange` (rangeset.ts:70-73: called "at the point where the ranges used to be split") and of `compareRange` (positions "in the new document", rangeset.ts:64-66), against code that compares positions of two documents; the run of the patched cm6.
reference: cm6 6.7.6 with `a.openEnd(end)` replaced by `a.openEnd(end - dPos)` at rangeset.ts:889.
note: The patch was run on chunk `rangeset` on 2026-11-19. F5046, listed by state.cm6.188.d2, does not change under it; that Ferrum with the correction gives F5046's record in bytes is deduced from the code (the comparison then stays in one document, and the conversion keeps order), not run. A missed call can leave a split drawn where the ranges merged inside a span nothing else redraws; a spurious one asks for a redraw of nothing. Not yet known: whether a consumer in `ferrum-view` relies on the spurious calls.

title: A mapped chunk's `maxPoint` counts only the points it keeps
cm6: `Chunk.map` raises the chunk's `maxPoint` for every mapped point before it decides whether the point stays in the chunk or spills into a lower layer (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:153, :155), so a chunk can carry the size of a point it does not hold (fixtures F0133, F0135, F0137, F5017).
better: Point-only scans (`minPointSize`, the heightmap) and `compare`'s sharing of chunks without points (`findSharedChunks`, rangeset.ts:571) would skip such a chunk.
basis: The code's order, run on cm6 6.7.6 (moving the count into the two branches that keep the point changes F0133, F0135, F0137 and F5017).
when: not evaluated again unless gate G8 of ferrum-state conformance measures such chunks in a point-only scan
reference: cm6 with the count moved after the keep-or-spill decision at rangeset.ts:155.
note: Declined: nobody gains from it. A chunk `map` builds is a new allocation, so it is never shared with the set it was mapped from; the over-count can only keep a later point scan or comparison from skipping one chunk of at most 250 ranges. Correcting it would change which chunks a later `compare` shares, and so which ranges its comparator is given, with no result a person editing or an application could name as better. Reopened by a measurement at gate G8 that shows such chunks in a point-only scan.

title: A sequential spec's own effects are mapped through the identity of their own document
cm6: `mergeTransaction` maps a sequential spec's own effects through `ChangeSet.empty(b.changes.length)` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/transaction.ts:314, :324), whose length is that of the document before the spec's changes, while those effects hold positions in the document after them. An effect type with a `map` whose value lies beyond the earlier document's length makes `update` throw `Position <pos> is out of range for changeset of length <len>`, and a `map` function reads that earlier length as the mapping's `length` and `newLength`.
better: A valid transaction (a sequential spec inserting text, then an effect at the end of the text it inserted) does not throw, and a `map` function is given a mapping of the document its value is in.
basis: None verified yet: no comment, CHANGELOG entry (mirrors/cm6/state/CHANGELOG.md has no entry on `sequential`) or test of cm6 says the length is meant. `extendTransaction` builds the same merge with a spec resolved against `tr.changes.newLength` (transaction.ts:397), where the two lengths agree, which reads as the intent.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to transaction.ts:314 (`ChangeSet.empty(b.changes.newLength)`), if adopted.
note: Found by the consultant while deciding Q112 (2026-11-19). Until then Ferrum reproduces cm6 with lengths in bytes. Under D1 the boundary of the throw compares a position of one document with the length of another, so for non-ASCII text it can fall at a different place than cm6's (doc "ab", a sequential spec inserting "é" at 0, an own effect at 2: cm6 maps it, Ferrum's 3 bytes exceed 2); no recorded fixture reaches the difference (of the fixtures of B2, F0561, F2067 and F2068 hold a sequential spec's own effect, each within the earlier length, and F0562 none). A fresh-seed fixture of conformance that does is no evidence against Ferrum and is a question there. The hazard of state.TransactionSpec.sequential.B2 says "beyond the doc": the doc is the one before the spec's changes.

title: A negative skip before a partial cursor's first `next` skips no text of the range
cm6: `PartialTextCursor.next` raises a negative `skip` to `from - pos` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:507-511), which before the first `next` is positive, and `nextInner` then adds `from - pos` again (text.ts:490-493): `iterRange(2, 14).next(-1)` on "one\u2028two…" returns "two", skipping "e\u2028", text inside the range (F6034, `firstNegative`).
better: A caller that asks to move back before reading anything reads the range from its start, and in Ferrum no skip given before the first `next` can land inside a character and panic (`state.cm6.225.d2`).
basis: Deduced from the code: the two additions of `from - pos` are each meant to bring the cursor to the range (one clips a skip, one moves to `from`), and applied together they count the distance twice. Not run; no CHANGELOG entry or test of cm6 found on it.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to text.ts:508 that keeps a negative skip from becoming positive (`skip = Math.max(skip, Math.min(0, this.from - this.pos))`, and its mirror for a backward cursor), if adopted; run on chunk `text` to see which fixtures change.
note: Raised by the implementer of U4 code as Q117 (2026-11-19). No mirrored consumer calls `next` with a negative skip on a cursor of `iterRange` before its first `next` (a deduction from the call sites to check at the delta).

title: A skip given to a reverse partial cursor counts from where the cursor stands, toward its range's start
cm6: `PartialTextCursor.next` clips a skip by the forward bounds whatever the direction (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:508-509), and `nextInner` raises it by `pos - to` (text.ts:496). On a reverse cursor a positive skip before the first `next` is cancelled, so the cursor reads from the document's end, outside the range: `iterRange(12, 2).next(2)` returns "four" at 15-19 (F0870, F0872, F0873); after the first `next` a positive skip is limited by the distance already travelled (`to - pos`) rather than the distance left (F0871).
better: A caller that iterates a range backwards with a skip gets text of the range, at the place the skip names, as `iterRange`'s documentation says ("Iterate over a range of the text", text.ts:105-107; a skip counts "positions after the current position", text.ts:16-18). In Ferrum every distance is then measured on the stretch it is walked over, so the place reached converts exactly between units and the panic and the other text of `state.cm6.225.d3` disappear.
basis: cm6's own documentation of `iterRange` and of `next(skip)` against the recorded values of state.TextIterator.next.B8 (F0870 to F0873). Not run; no CHANGELOG entry or test of cm6 found on it.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to text.ts:508-509 that clips a skip by the bounds of the cursor's direction (`pos - from` for a positive skip on a reverse cursor, and the mirror for a negative one), written and run with the patch of `state.imp.016`, which touches the same lines, on chunk `text` and on G5's cases of `state.cm6.225.d2` and `.d3` to see which fixtures change.
note: Raised by the U1 conformance verifier as Q136 (2026-11-24). No mirrored consumer passes a skip to an iterRange or iterLines cursor (state.TextIterator.next.B8 consumer_values; to check again at the delta). If declined, the panic of state.cm6.225.d2 and .d3 on a call where cm6 returns a value is below cm6's floor of stability (D13, Q128) and needs its own answer at the same point.

title: A change description serialized without building a JSON value of every section
cm6: `ChangeDesc.toJSON()` returns its own `sections` array (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:167), so the call costs nothing and the caller's `JSON.stringify` pays for the text. Ferrum's `to_json` builds a `serde_json::Value` of every number (crates/ferrum-state/src/change.rs:263-265; N9), a copy that `state.cm6.229.d1` requires so that the caller cannot change the description: 69.5 ms for 10^6 sections at G8 (conformance/g8-growth.txt), where cm6's call takes 8.8 ns.
better: An application that persists or sends changes (history, collaboration) writes their JSON text straight from the description, with one pass and no intermediate value of every number; the call that returns a `Value` stays for those that need one.
basis: G8's timed run of 2026-11-27 (Q144) on the call alone; the pair of the round of step 5 (`to_json` then `serde_json::to_string`, against cm6's `toJSON` then `JSON.stringify`) measures what a caller pays end to end.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: None needed for the text: it must equal `serde_json::to_string(&desc.to_json())` byte for byte on every fixture of `ChangeDesc.toJSON` and `ChangeSet.toJSON`; the time is measured by G8's pair.
note: An added function (a writer of the JSON text, or a `Serialize` view of the description) breaks no caller, so it waits for the delta (D16). N9 declined `Serialize` on the types themselves because it would be a second serialized form; a form whose text is defined as the `Value`'s is not a second form, which the delta weighs against N9's reason.

title: `invert` refuses a document whose length is not the set's
cm6: `ChangeSet.invert` takes "the document as it existed before the changes" (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:214-217) and does not check its length (:218-232; Q11, `state.cm6.140.d1` reproduces it). A shorter document gives a set whose insertions claim text it lacks ([2,[3,""],2], F0353); mapped, that set loses the empty text, and its `toJSON`, `compose` and `apply` then fail with an engine `TypeError` (F8018, `state.ChangeSet.invert.B3`). A longer document gives a well-formed set holding slices of the wrong text, with no failure anywhere (F0354).
better: A caller that passes the wrong document learns it at the call that took it, with a message naming the mismatch, as `apply` already does for the same mistake (change.ts:208), instead of a failure at a later, unrelated call (Q152's panic) or, with a longer document, an undo that silently restores the wrong text. History and collaboration, which invert every change, are where the longer-document case would corrupt a document unseen.
basis: cm6's own documentation of `invert` (the document before the changes, which has the set's length) and its check of the same condition in `apply`; the failures recorded in F0353, F0354 and F8018. No CHANGELOG entry or test of cm6 found on it; no mirrored caller passes another document.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to change.ts:218 throwing `RangeError("Inverting change set against a document with the wrong length")` when `doc.length != this.length`, run on every fixture by `tools/oracle_patch.py`: the fixtures it changes must be those of `state.ChangeSet.invert.B2` and `.B3` and no other.
note: Raised by the consultant from Q152 (2026-11-27). If adopted, no input of the public API builds a set with a missing text, and the panic `The change set holds no text for one of its insertions` (design.md §5) is removed with its `# Panics` texts in the same delta, its site then UNREACHABLE. Weighed against: a panic where cm6 returns a set, which a caller relying on cm6's leniency would meet; none is known.
